A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same REP framework, with readable text, equations, figures and tables. v4 includes Appendices A–N. v2 ends after its references and mentions a separate supplement that is not embedded; comparisons therefore concern the supplied content, not when unprovided experiments were first performed.

before.justification: v2 reports original continual-learning experiments, resource measurements, component ablations and sensitivity results on CIFAR-100, ImageNet-R and PlantDisease.

after.justification: v4 retains original experiments and reports additional method comparisons, dataset evaluations, sensitivity studies and Jetson energy measurements in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The original surrogate selection, AToM scheduler and ALD procedure are retained; v2's Algorithms 1–2 reappear in v4 Appendix A. A limited procedural extension appears in Section 4.3.1, which integrates ConvPrompt into SLCA to enable parameter-efficient adaptation before applying REP. Expanded descriptions of projection and baseline losses do not independently establish changes to the original REP procedure.

E1.justification: The three original datasets and class-incremental classification setting remain. v4 adds Split CUB-200 bird classification and evaluation on subsets of 5-datasets in Appendices G and K. The latter subsets are not identified precisely. Changes to task-sequence splits are protocol changes rather than additional dataset coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated prompting methods expand from L2P, DualPrompt and CODA-Prompt to include HiDe-Prompt, ConvPrompt, LAE and OVOR, including in the corresponding original-setup comparison. v4 also reports comparisons involving SLCA, RanPAC, Online-LoRA, ADAM variants, F-OAL and Miro. The BudgetCL and MEMO comparisons remain in Appendix D.

E3.justification: The principal computational metric changes from total GPU wall-clock time to iteration time, and surrogate similarity changes from CCA to CKA. Additional protocols include five-task splits, broader twenty-task evaluations, self-supervised backbone configurations, computation-budget sweeps and energy-matched Jetson comparisons. Newly disclosed batch sizes and training recipes do not establish that retained experiments changed or were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations, v4 tests intermediate-layer prompt selection, FIM-based merging and several random-drop rates. It expands token-merging and layer-keeping sweeps, extends ablations to additional methods and CIFAR-100, and adds threshold, prompt-pool and computation-budget analyses in Appendices E, K and L.

E5.justification: v2 displays uncertainty values without identifying their meaning or repetition count. v4's checklist explicitly states five repetitions and reporting of means and standard deviations. This adds statistical reporting information; it does not establish an increase in runs. Appendix K also documents five-fold cross-validation.

E6.justification: v4 adds extensive accuracy, forgetting, resource and energy results. Shared entries also change: in the original-setup ImageNet-R comparison, L2P accuracy changes from 61.57 to 59.7 and CODA-Prompt from 75.45 to 70.5 (v2 Table 5; v4 Table 10). These are revised reported results, not established method improvements. The 76.3% CCA result and approximately 97% CKA result use different metrics.

T1.justification: REP's retrieval rule and adaptive merging and dropping schedules retain their mathematical substance. v4's generalized loss notation and Appendix B baseline formulas expand the explanation of evaluated methods rather than establish new theoretical reasoning. Neither version provides theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: v2 centers its contribution on efficient prompt-based continual learning. v4's introduction explicitly extends the claimed applicability beyond prompting to other rehearsal-free methods. It also revises headline efficiency claims from 16–47% training-time and 5–33% memory reductions to maxima of 51% and 41% for prompting, with separate claims for the additional methods.

C2.justification: v4 softens the direct identification of local attention with task-specific knowledge and adds explanations for surrogate alternatives and RanPAC's memory bottleneck. It introduces substantive qualifications concerning hyperparameter tuning, comparison with online F-OAL, and surveillance misuse. The earlier curriculum and replay-buffer discussion is retained and expanded.

D1.justification: Appendices B, D, K and M supply optimizer settings, learning rates, batch size, iteration budgets, CNN training details, tuning procedures and Jetson power-measurement instructions absent from the supplied v2. The reference GPU is stated as RTX 3090 rather than RTX 3090 Ti. The checklist newly reports a supplementary code archive, whose availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v4 substantially broadens research positioning through discussion and citations concerning ConvPrompt, LAE, SLCA, Online-LoRA, F-OAL and self-supervised pretraining. Appendix J adds comparisons with online or few-shot learning and neural architecture search. Previously cited HiDe-Prompt and OVOR receive fuller treatment rather than constituting entirely new references.

P1.justification: The main text is extensively rewritten and reorganized. Section 3 separates challenges, solutions and backbone analysis; the preliminary CNN comparison moves to Appendix D; and the brief discussion becomes a conclusion with expanded limitations. These changes substantially alter the narrative independently of the added experiments.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to a single-column conference layout. v2's best-method Figure 6 gives way to extensive paired-result tables; Figure 5 moves to Appendix D and gains PlantDisease panels. Figure 4 is redrawn with additional strategies, algorithms move to Appendix A, and new tables and device-energy figures substantially expand the displays.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2's best-method summaries and unembedded supplementary detail, v4's paired comparisons, targeted controls, sensitivity studies and included Jetson measurements substantially strengthen assessment of REP's applicability and practical efficiency. Training recipes and explicit run reporting improve reproducibility. New reporting inconsistencies weaken individual findings: Table 3 lists FIM at 264 ms versus AToM at 419 ms while claiming FIM increases training time. These problems do not outweigh the broader gains in evidential support and transparency.
